parsed.doc_summary: Berkeley Ordinance 7,992-N.S. amends BMC ch. 13.63, prohibiting sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Passed to print Nov 18, 2025; no effective date stated in the text.

rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with attorney's fees to a prevailing party.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation); damages, injunctive relief, restitution, attorney's fees
rules.effective_date_note: Ordinance text states no effective date; passed to print Nov 18, 2025 (adoption expected Dec 2, 2025 per URL). Other sources may give a different date.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in this document; other sources publish differing dates (e.g., March 1, 2026 vs. January 2026). This ordinance amends an existing chapter 13.63.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, market research for financing, appraisals, and software research/testing/training.
